Managing Elements

Elements are added through a page's Children collection or the window's Elements collection. Each element can only belong to one owner at a time.

Adding and Removing Elements

Removing an element and disposing it are separate operations. Removing it allows you to keep the object and use it again, for example in a cache:

  • Add: Attaches an element that is not currently owned or disposed. Duplicate ownership and cycles are rejected.
  • Remove / Clear: Detaches elements without disposing them. You are responsible for cleaning them up if they are no longer needed.
  • IsVisible=false: Hides the element while keeping it attached and preserving its state.
  • Dispose: Detaches the element and releases its resources. Calling it again is safe, but the element cannot be reused afterwards.
  • Window Disposal: Stops the window and disposes roots that are still attached. Detached elements remain your responsibility.

Removing from Another Thread

When the window is running, RequestRemove can be called to queue removal on the UI thread:

The request applies to the current attachment. If the element or one of its parents is detached and reused before the request runs, the old request is ignored. RequestRemove does not dispose the element.

Like other queued work, a new request is rejected while the window is stopping.

Lifetime Methods

Custom controls can override these methods to manage subscriptions and resources:

  • OnAttachedToWindow: Subscribe to the current window and start window-specific work.
  • OnDetachedFromWindow: Remove those subscriptions and stop window-specific work, while keeping the element reusable.
  • OnChildAdded / OnChildRemoved: Update any layout or tracking information held by a container.
  • DisposeCore: Permanently release resources owned by the element.

Call the base implementation when extending an existing container. Keep these methods synchronous and avoid throwing during cleanup. Bindings managed by MelonUI suspend on detach and resume on reattachment; event subscriptions you add yourself need your own cleanup.
